![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/9f94742a7f37fd7f6a1c789401a2e323fec80aca584774453cba03cf69f28ade.png)

Consider the vector field $F$ shown above, and let $C$ be the path along the segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$

III. ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is false, while statement II is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$  works against the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/f4e8c62562ee1657e41bb36a21c901dc95935558641f724f934a4c58706f4a64.png)

 

So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

- Statement III is true. It's clear from the picture below that if we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves from $B$ to $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/40b100dd4bc71b95f5ad99eb0cec8ed87133211bb371b22deccb851f79c695b3.png)

 

So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
